shadows.value: squircle in #0E2A1E at 26% opacity, Gaussian blur stdDeviation 9, offset 0 10px
shadows.purpose: The macOS icon body's single soft drop shadow.

shadows.value: 2px #0E2A1E hairline at 10% plus a 5px inner white rim fading 75% to 0 over the top 35%

components.name: Menu-Bar Glyph: alarm states

narrative.overview:
Every location check is an entry stamp: the internet admits this Mac somewhere, and Whereabouts inks where. The mark is a tilted, double-bordered violet rubber stamp on a pale mint visa page with guilloché security print. It holds an entry arrow arriving at a point, with WHEREABOUTS across the top and ADMITTED beneath. The ink is uneven, as a real stamp's would be: heavy at one corner, thin at the far one, eroded at the edges, with paper showing through. Two faint, older green impressions carrying place codes bleed off the page edges. They are the history of where this Mac has been seen.

The brand world covers three carriers and nothing else: the app icon (`Resources/AppIcon.icns`), the menu-bar status glyph (`StampGlyph.swift`), and the wordmark lockup (`Branding/wordmark*.svg`). All three are drawn from one measured geometry in `Branding/brand.py`. The glyph reuses the icon's stamp proportions, its arrow-into-point mark, and its -7° tilt. The in-app SwiftUI windows (Settings, Status) are deliberately not part of this world. They follow native macOS conventions: system colors, SF Symbols, and grouped forms. No app-UI tokens exist, so don't invent any.

The mark refuses the category defaults (shield, padlock, globe with a pin on a blue gradient) and makes a clean break from GeoMeister's metal compass and teal.
keyCharacteristics: One stamp, three carriers: icon, menu-bar glyph, and wordmark all share the stamp's frame ratio (about 1.41:1), its -7° tilt, and the arrow-into-point mark.
Ink carries meaning; color is never decoration.
Lettering is stroke-built condensed monoline caps on a 10-unit grid. The mark ships with no font.
Two detail levels: full (lettering, guilloché, ghost stamps, ink texture) at 128px and up; small (frame plus mark only) at 64px and below.
Calm states draw light and alarms draw heavy: in the menu bar, a problem always looks heavier than an all-clear.

rules.name: The One Ink, One Law Rule
rules.body: Each ink has one meaning. Violet is the brand at rest. Green means admitted. In the menu bar, system red means refused or blocked, system orange means leak, and system gray means unknown, offline, or checking. Never use an ink for a meaning it does not carry.

rules.name: The System Colors in the Menu Bar Rule
rules.body: The status glyph never uses brand hexes. In colored mode it uses `systemGreen`, `systemRed`, `systemOrange`, and `systemGray`. Otherwise it is a template image that follows the menu bar's appearance.

rules.name: The No-Font Rule
rules.body: The mark is never set in a system or web font. New lettering adds glyphs to the stroke grid (10-unit cap, 1.75 stroke, flat-clipped diagonals) instead of substituting a typeface.

rules.name: The Legibility Scale Rule
rules.body: The full stamp is 664 × 470px, about 80% of the squircle width (81%). Its tilted bounds are about 87% (716px). The surface brief records that as 85%; the build measures 87%. The stamp was enlarged from the contract's 70% so the lettering stays legible at the 128px slot. Don't shrink it back toward 70%. The small stamp is 700 × 500px (85% of the body width) so the frame stays heavy at 16-64px.

rules.name: The Two Detail Levels Rule
rules.body: The `.icns` 16, 32 and 64px slots use `icon-small.svg`: frame and arrow-into-point only, with no lettering, guilloché, ghosts, or ink texture. The 128px slot and larger use `icon.svg`. `Branding/build.sh` enforces this split.

rules.name: The Imperfect Impression Rule
rules.body: Pressure falloff, erosion, and voids belong to the full-detail stamp only. Small sizes and the menu-bar glyph are clean, solid ink.

rules.name: The Heavier-When-Wrong Rule
rules.body: Calm states are an inked outline. Alarms are a solid stamp with the mark cut out. An empty frame means there is nothing to attest yet.

rules.name: The Kill Switch Outranks Rule
rules.body: State precedence is kill switch, then leak, then geo state. While a leak is active, the glyph never shows admitted.

dos: Do derive every brand asset from `Branding/brand.py` and regenerate through `Branding/build.sh`. Never hand-edit the SVGs or the `.icns`.
Do keep the full stamp at about 80% of the squircle width so the lettering reads at 128px.
Do use the small detail level at 64px and below.
Do keep the -7° tilt and the arrow-into-point mark consistent across icon, glyph, and wordmark.
Do use system colors (or a template image) for the menu-bar glyph, and give every state its accessibility label.
Do keep the in-app windows native macOS.
donts: Don't use shields, padlocks, globes with pins, or blue gradients, and don't bring back the GeoMeister compass or teal.
Don't set the mark's lettering in a font.
Don't use a brand ink for a meaning it does not carry, or put brand hexes in the menu bar.
Don't show an all-clear glyph while a leak, violation, or kill switch is active.
Don't apply guilloché, ghost stamps, lettering, or ink erosion below 128px.
Don't replace the custom status glyph with SF Symbols.
